content.coverIntro: Verkerk Versdistributie B.V. supplies fruit and vegetables to restaurants and smaller supermarkets, in blue returnable crates that have to come back. This proposal focuses on one concrete problem: the crate balance per customer is not reliable, so Verkerk only discovers each quarter that thousands of crates are 'missing' and cannot back up that difference with the customer.
content.situation: Every driver makes the delivery and is supposed to get a slip signed showing how many crates he drops off and how many he takes back. In practice the eleven drivers fill this in with varying accuracy; slips get lost. At the end of the week Nienke and Sven type the slips into an Excel file per customer: together about five hours a week, just the typing alone. Even then the balances still don't add up. Last quarter the Excel showed 1,800 crates outstanding at customers, spread across 93 customers. The biggest customer, a supermarket chain with six branches, said it only had 950 crates. A difference of 850 crates, which at €8-10 per crate easily comes to €6,800-8,500 at that one customer alone. Without reliable data of its own, Verkerk cannot back up that difference and most of it is written off as a loss. Crates are not recorded digitally anywhere; AFAS is only used for invoicing.
goals: See the current crate balance per customer, per week, instead of only discovering each quarter that it is wrong
Step in before a crate discrepancy gets out of hand, instead of having a 'yes you did, no we didn't' argument with the customer afterwards
Reduce the structural crate loss in euros: crates that sit at customers but are not reported back
Free up the five hours a week that Nienke and Sven now spend typing
Be able to put a substantiated crate balance per customer on the table in quarterly meetings with big customers
content.approach: We connect AFAS for deliveries per customer and build a crate balance overview on top of it: for each customer, every delivery is matched against the crates that come back, so the outstanding balance is always correct rather than only at quarter close. The drivers keep working as they do now, on paper; no scanners or apps are added. The slips remain the source, but are no longer typed over: they are submitted digitally and automatically read into crate lines per customer per delivery. Where a slip is missing or unclear, the overview flags it as an open item instead of silently turning it into a number. This way Nienke sees the current crate balance per customer every week, with the underlying deliveries alongside it, and can step in before a discrepancy builds up. The overview can also be shared separately with Kees for the quarterly meetings with big accounts.
scopeDeliverables: Connection to AFAS for deliveries per customer, with customer number matching so crate lines are attached to the right customer
Digital submission of the drivers' slips and automatic reading into crate lines (delivered and returned) per customer per delivery
Crate balance overview per customer per week: outstanding balance, underlying deliveries, and the difference from the previous period
Flagging of missing or unclear slips as open items, instead of silent correction
Alert flag for customers whose balance exceeds an agreed threshold
Weekly automatic refresh of the overview
Separately shareable overview for Kees for quarterly meetings with big customers
Short guide for Nienke and Sven on the weekly submission of slips so the processing keeps working

phases.name: Week 1: scoping and data connection
phases.description: Set up the AFAS connection for deliveries per customer, align customer number matching, and define the fixed format for submitting slips.

phases.name: Week 2-3: build reading and overview
phases.description: Build the automatic reading of slips into crate lines, and set up the crate balance overview per customer per week with alert flags and open items.

phases.name: Week 4: test and deliver
phases.description: Run one cycle with real slips and AFAS deliveries, adjust based on feedback from Nienke and Sven, and deliver the overview including the separately shareable version for Kees.

content.investment: This project is scoped as one clearly defined problem - the reliable crate balance per customer per week - at a fixed price. We will confirm the exact investment after a short scoping call in which we go through the AFAS setup, the slip format and the desired threshold together.
content.nextSteps: Approval of this proposal, followed by a short scoping call (about 30 minutes) with Nienke and Sven to go through the AFAS connection, the slip format and the alert threshold. After that we start straight away in week 1.
